Sanjay: FYI I woke up to a ~12% p99 regression on decode-heavy traffic after yesterday's kernel selector + batching tweak. I put a short profile in the thread, want quick eyes before we escalate :eyes:
Anya: Oh no — any obvious KV hit-rate change?
Sanjay: KV hit-rate dropped ~6pp for long-context (8k) requests. Perf log + bench command below:
Sanjay: ```
./tools/bench --workload=chat --seq=8192 --concurrency=32 --profile=flame --out=prof.json
--kernel=auto-v2 --batcher=continuous
# p50 18ms -> 19.5ms, p99 240ms -> 269ms (decode-dominated requests)
# kv_hit: 0.72 -> 0.66
```
Mike: That smells like the continuous batch formation now mixing prefill tokens and decode tokens in the same microbatch more often. If decode steps land in a kernel that expects warm kv-cache but sees cold entries, kernel path costs spike.
Anya: Can you dump a short trace of phase composition (prefill vs decode) per batch for the failing run? Even a rough histogram helps.
Sanjay: Posted a tiny CSV of batch phases attached — most microbatches went 60% prefill + 40% decode, previously it was 95%/5% for these workloads. Looks like the batching window widened.
Julia: This aligns with the scheduler's jitter change — we increased batch wait from 4ms -> 8ms to improve throughput. That increases mixing probability for split-phase flows.
Kevin: Proposed quick experiments: 1) enforce strict phase-siloing for 2 minutes (separate queues for prefill vs decode), 2) raise KV warmup grace (prefetch keepalive) from 50ms -> 200ms, 3) pin kernel affinity for decode to the lower-latency kernel.
Anya: I can run 1+2 on canary now. If isolate-prefill is good, we'll know it's mixing.
infra-bot: deployer: canary rollout triggered for bench-experiments/split-queues (id: c-2026-03-18).
Mike: Another hypothesis: token-budget target recalculation moved some requests into a larger batch shape that picks different kernel (matmul tiling more expensive for decode). We should log kernel selection per batch (model, seq_len, effective_batch_shape).
Sanjay: Added a quick patch that logs kernel choice to bench output. Running it now, will post results in ~10m.
Anya: If separate queues fixes p99 but hurts throughput, we can try phase-aware batching heuristics: e.g., prefer same-phase coalescing but allow cross-phase if wait exceeds X ms or if token budget underutilized.
Julia: Agreed — we had a prior config `phase_prefer=0.8` (0..1). Maybe tune to 0.95 for decode-heavy endpoints.
Kevin: Note: we should also check for perf regressions introduced by the kernel selector fallback path for decode. Last week we added a fallback that switches kernels when sequence length > 4k; maybe fallback cost higher than previous.
Sanjay: Preliminary logged sample: batch_id=1753, seq=8192, chosen_kernel=kv-optimized-v1, fallback_kernel=matmul-fast-v2, kernel_switch_cost_ms=6.7
Mike: 6.7ms extra can matter at p99. If it's per-batch and we have many small decode batches that all flip, it accumulates.
Anya: Results from canary (split queues + kv-warmup=200ms): p99 back to baseline within noise (+1%). KV hit restored to 0.71. Throughput down ~3% for combined workload.
Sanjay: Good signal: mixing was the culprit. Next steps: revert the global batch-wait increase, implement phase-aware preference (configurable per-route), add kernel-selection logging and a metric for kernel_switch_count.
Julia: I'll open a tiny RFC for a phase_pref parameter and default to 0.9 for high-latency models.
Kevin: I'll follow up to add kernel_switch_count to the telemetry dashboard and an alert if > 1% of batches switch kernel.
Sanjay: Action items summarized: 
- Julia: RFC for phase_pref and rollout plan (PR + canary)
- Kevin: telemetry + alert for kernel_switch_count
- Anya: run longer A/B with phase_pref=0.95 vs 0.85 for 24h
- Mike: benchmark microbatch shapes to see where kernel selector flips most often
infra-bot: ticket created: PERF-4127 "split-batch phase preference tuning + kernel switch telemetry"
Julia: Thanks all, nice quick triage. Keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
